A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARXIV2TABLE work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including material relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original table-generation experiments with five LLMs, retrieval results, an iteration ablation and human-validation outcomes.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results, including Table 2, the iteration study, human validation and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The method retains full-text information extraction, randomized batches of four papers, five iterations of selection and schema refinement, and final full-text value verification. The QA evaluation procedure is also unchanged; Figure 4's redesign does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ARXIV2TABLE corpus of 1,957 tables referencing 7,158 papers, with the same distractor-based selection and table-generation tasks. No additional dataset, domain or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Method 1, Method 2 and Method 3 are renamed Baseline 1, Baseline 2 and Newman et al., respectively. Their procedures and participation in the main, human-validation and cost comparisons remain unchanged, as do the five backbone models.

E3.justification: Section 6.3 changes the reported metric set for the retained GPT-4o iteration study: paper-selection recall is replaced by average schema, unary-value and pairwise-value F1. The one-to-five iteration range and other evaluation settings remain unchanged; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The iteration ablation no longer shows how paper-selection recall varies with iteration count, instead adding aggregate table-quality F1 alongside the retained component curves. Human-validation analyses, computational comparisons and Appendix C case studies remain present.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 states in both versions that experiments are repeated twice and average performance is reported. No seed disclosure, confidence interval, significance test or other uncertainty-reporting practice is added or removed.

E6.justification: Table 2's numerical results and the human-validation results are unchanged. The ablation drops the paper-recall trajectory and adds a mean-F1 trajectory; its three retained F1 curves match across versions. Computational success-rate differences are equivalent rounding, such as 48.19% becoming 48.2%.

T1.justification: The task formalization in Section 3 and similarity-based distractor-ranking equation in Section 4.2 are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a more realistic benchmark, utilization-based QA evaluation and iterative table generation. Claims about task difficulty, method effectiveness and novelty retain their scope.

C2.justification: v3 removes the assertion that reduced prompt-content overlap ensures fairer evaluation and the footnote explaining why missing relevant papers motivates prioritizing recall over precision. The mechanism discussions, iteration interpretation and limitations concerning GPT-4o dependence, contamination and generalizability remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The appendices retain the prompts, model checkpoints, access methods, context limits and generation temperature. Code and dataset access information is unchanged. Computational details move from Section 6.5 to Appendix A.3 rather than being newly disclosed or removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Padmakumar et al. (2025), 'Setting the Table with Intent,' to the related-work discussion and bibliography. This is a limited citation addition; the broader positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 renames the baselines, selectively shortens explanations, moves computational-cost discussion into Appendix A.3 and adds acknowledgments. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 becomes a compact evaluation-only diagram, removing its generation-workflow panel. The iteration plot is rescaled and relabeled, the model-comparison bar chart moves to the appendix, and several tables are resized, reordered or relocated. Most visual content remains intact.

improvement.justification: The benchmark, method, main results, human validation, computational evidence and reproducibility details are retained. v3 makes aggregate F1 and the evaluation flow more explicit, but loses the paper-recall trajectory and generation-workflow illustration. Together with limited prose editing and one added citation, these changes leave the paper's overall evidential strength and quality essentially unchanged.
